passage: Home visit note, Thursday. Pema, two, saw the plate and backed against the wall. Her father Varun followed her round the room with a spoon, saying, "One more or no toy." Pema clamped her lips and cried, hands over her face. I asked Varun to eat beside her, with two small pieces on her plate to take or leave. By the end Pema had reached over and taken a piece of roti from his plate herself. I will return next week.

qa.q: What did Varun say as he followed Pema with the spoon?
qa.a: He said, "One more or no toy."

qa.q: What was Pema feeling when she backed against the wall at the sight of the plate?
qa.a: She seemed frightened, since she clamped her lips, cried and hid her face, so food had become something to dread.

qa.q: What did the visitor suggest to change mealtimes?
qa.a: Sit and eat together, offer two small pieces on her plate, and let Pema choose whether to take them.

qa.q: How might Varun have been feeling while chasing Pema with the spoon?
qa.a: He was probably worried that she was not eating enough and afraid of being a poor parent, and that worry came out as pressure.

grounding: Shows a toddler frightened by chasing and threats at mealtime, and a visitor guiding the father to offer food and eat together.
